messages:
devin: ran perf on kg-node-3 today, attached perf.data from a 120s steady-state workload. seeing ~22% CPU in our python scheduler loop even with C-backed queue ops — surprised how hot tokenization is too.

maria: can you paste the perf-top output or flamegraph link?

devin: uploaded perf script output to /tmp/perf-1791012345.svg (public on ci-artifacts for now). key lines: 
```
# perf top -n 20
22.1%  python  [.] handle_batch
13.5%  libtokenizer.so [.] tokenize_span
9.8%   python  [.] schedule_requests
8.0%   libc-2.31 [.] memcpy
```

sam: hmm, libtokenizer.so eating 13% makes me think our fastpath isn't hit for short prompts. what's the input length distribution?

devin: 80% < 32 tokens, we still see repeated memcpy and fallback utf8 path. I reran with flamegraph (perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl) — big Python frames on top of C tokenizer frames.

olga: could be GIL contention from threadpool + many tiny batches. did you profile with 'perf record -g -p PID' or system-wide?

devin: system-wide (-a) to capture kernel+user. also tried per-thread on the scheduler: `perf record -g -p $(pidof runtime_scheduler) -o sched.data -- sleep 60` shows scheduler loop: PyObject_Call -> schedule_one -> handle_batch -> process_kv_cache.

maria: any evidence kernel selection costs? e.g., context switches to run blocking IO or cuda driver wakeups?

devin: nvtx traces were clean — GPU idle time low. But perf shows sporadic context-switches when cache miss triggers file-backed mmap in kvcache.c. That shows up as page faults (~2.4% cost) and syscall overhead.

sam: possible mitigation: pre-touch kv cache pages and move mmap into loader thread to avoid hitting scheduler path. Also consider switching tokenizer to single-threaded C hotpath for short sequences.

devin: tried pre-touch in a branch (pr/3587) — reduced page-faults by ~60% and scheduler Python CPU went from 22% -> 14% in a short run. flamegraph before/after shows much smaller PyEval frames.

infra-bot: deploy bot: canary deployed pr/3587 to canary-kg-2 at 03:20 UTC, rollout id r-2026-03-15-kkv

maria: great. next step: run a larger perfetto capture (20s) to confirm no regressions in batching latency percentile. Also run stress with many tiny requests to validate no regressions under high QPS.

devin: agreed. I'll schedule perfetto on canary and attach timeline. will post the trace and a short note on which symbols were trimmed.

olga: also add a small unit test to simulate repeated small prompts to ensure tokenizer fastpath stays covered in CI. small PR pls.

devin: yep. opening follow-up PR for tokenizer fastpath tests and adding kv pre-touch toggle behind env var.

sam: nice detective work. :trophy:

maria: thanks! once perfetto trace is up I'll close the loop and add a rollout note in the release channel.
